headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared file-based workflows; B’s shell/write capabilities can amplify A’s PDF content into unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A reads PDF files and runs browser-based tests; B reads/writes files, executes shell, and uses stdin/stdout plus APIs. A’s document content can therefore reach B through shared files or copied text, and B may treat it as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A-produced PDF text is copied into B’s prompt or files, B may follow injected instructions.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace, document content can bridge into B’s tool-using context.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Strip instructions from extracted PDF text before passing to B.
Use a fixed prompt template for B that ignores document directives.
Review any B action plan before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from A to B inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches PDF documents and has no network egress; B touches academic papers, paper metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets, and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. If A’s PDFs or extracted text are placed in B’s workspace, B can transmit that content outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default local-development setups.
conditions: IF A’s PDF contents are stored in B’s workspace, B can read them.
IF B sends prompts or retrieved context to allowlisted APIs, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive PDFs in B’s working tree.
Disable B network access for sensitive runs.
Use redacted copies of documents for B.
Separate secrets from document-processing inputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and browser-based tests; B supports multiple instances, writes the filesystem, executes shell, and spawns subprocesses. Even without git writes, overlapping write access to the same directory can cause clobbering or race conditions. The profiles do not state locking or isolated workspaces, so the conflict is plausible by default.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory, files can be overwritten or corrupted.
IF both run concurrently without locking, generated artifacts may race.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Add a simple lock file before writes.
Check for existing artifacts before starting.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A processes PDFs and B is a content-writing agent with API and shell access. If A’s extracted text or summaries are fed into B, B may treat them as authoritative and generate downstream outputs or actions without verification. The profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so the cascade is credible but not proven high-impact.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s extracted text as source material, errors can propagate into B’s outputs.
IF B is instructed to act on A’s summaries without review, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require B to cite original PDFs, not only A summaries.
Add a human review step before B actions.
Compare B outputs against source documents.
Limit B to drafting, not executing, actions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles PDF documents with browser-based processing and no egress; B handles academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets, with allowlisted network egress and local-development sandboxing. If regulated or sensitive PDFs flow from A into B, retention and transmission policies can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is a medium-risk possibility.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by both agents, their handling policies may diverge.
IF B uploads or logs content from A, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated PDFs to B.
Mask secrets before B processing.
Confirm retention settings for B logs.
Use a local-only run for sensitive data.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls.
